title: なんて, なんか and など
summary: Three small words that mean "and so on" or "things like": など is neutral, なんて and なんか add surprise or a belittling tone.

blocks.text: These three words overlap, so a dictionary list of meanings feels random. Think of them as a scale from neutral to casual.

rows: "what a ...", surprise, downplaying, a vague という

blocks.text: **など** is not a cop-out like "etc." can be in English. It lists examples and sits right after the noun, even before other particles.

blocks.jp: 机の上に本やペンなどがある。
blocks.en: On the desk there are books, pens and so on.

blocks.text: In casual speech it can also make light of a noun: the speaker rejects "things like that".

blocks.en: (I) don't say flattery or the like.

blocks.text: なんか: things like, something, somehow

なんか is a squashed 何か (something). From "something" it grows: **vague** (なんか変だ), **for some reason** (なんか眠い), and in sloppy talk a filler like "kinda". Attached to a noun it belittles it, often with real feeling, and it is common with oneself.

blocks.en: I can't stand a person like my big brother.

blocks.jp: 私なんかには無理です。
blocks.en: Someone like me can't do that.

blocks.text: なんて: a squashed なんと / 何という
なんて asks "what?" (なんて言ったの？), but it is also the exclamation **"what a ...!"**, a belittling marker after a noun, and a surprise marker after a whole clause.

blocks.jp: なんて広い部屋なんだ。

blocks.en: I hate studying and things like it.

blocks.jp: 雪が降るなんて信じられない。
blocks.en: I can't believe it's snowing! (of all things)

blocks.jp: 田中なんて人は知らない。
blocks.en: I don't know anybody called Tanaka. (and I doubt there is one)

items: **など** is neutral, **なんて** is in the middle, **なんか** is the most casual.
After a noun, なんか and なんて belittle it and replace が and を.
After a whole clause, **なんて** shows surprise or disbelief; なんか never does that.

questions.prompt: かばんの中に本＿＿ノートなどがある。
questions.note: や lists examples, and など closes the list.
questions.en: In the bag there are books, notebooks and so on.

questions.instruction: Which one is the most casual?
questions.note: など is neutral, なんて is in the middle, なんか is the most casual.

questions.instruction: Which one is neutral and fine in formal writing?
questions.note: など sits right after the noun and suits formal writing.
なんて + noun phrase makes the exclamation "what a ...!".

questions.prompt: あんな人なんかに会いたくない。
questions.note: After a noun, なんか belittles it.
questions.en: I don't want to meet a person like that.

questions.instruction: What does なんか mean here?
questions.note: なんか at the start of a clause is a vague "somehow".
なんか after a noun belittles it and replaces を.
questions.en: I don't want to watch TV or the like.

questions.prompt: After a whole clause, なんか shows surprise or disbelief.
questions.note: Only なんて shows surprise after a whole clause.

questions.prompt: なんて can show surprise after a whole clause.
questions.note: After a clause, なんて means "I can't believe...".

questions.prompt: 雨が降るなんて思わなかった。
questions.note: なんて after a whole clause shows surprise.
questions.en: I never thought it would rain!

questions.note: なんか after a noun belittles it, often oneself.
なんて after a noun belittles it.
questions.en: I don't need friends or anything like that.

questions.instruction: Tap the word that means "and so on"
questions.note: など closes a list of examples.
questions.en: I bought books, notebooks and so on.

questions.note: なんて opens the exclamation.

questions.prompt: It's somehow hot today, isn't it.
questions.note: なんか: a vague "somehow" before the clause.
questions.en: It's somehow hot today, isn't it.

questions.prompt: I don't eat vegetables or anything like that.
questions.note: なんか after the noun replaces を and belittles it.
questions.en: I don't eat vegetables or anything like that.

questions.instruction: Which pair belittles a noun and can replace が / を?
options: なんか and なんて
questions.note: なんか and なんて are the belittling pair.

options: 箱の中にりんごやバナナなどがある
questions.note: や ... など lists examples.

questions.instruction: なんか is a squashed what?
questions.note: なんか is a squashed 何か, "something".

questions.instruction: なんて is a squashed what?
questions.note: なんて is a squashed なんと / 何という.

questions.prompt: 私なんかが先生になれない。
questions.note: なんか after 私 belittles oneself.
questions.en: Someone like me can't become a teacher.
